It distinguishes itself from image-level compositing by correctly handling occlusions between different channels, as it retains depth information that image-level blending discards [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the method distinguishes itself from image-level compositing by correctly handling occlusions between different channels because it retains depth information, which image-level blending discards. Source [S1] explicitly states that 'A problem that arises with image-level intermixing is that occlusions between different channels can not be handled correctly due to missing depth information in the accumulated intermediate results.' It further defines accumulation-level intermixing (which the author's method uses) as evaluating illumination models per channel and combining results, implying the retention of necessary information (like depth) during the accumulation process to avoid the issues seen in image-level blending. Thus, the evidence supports the claim.
